DESCRIPTION
  Our project aims to visualize and analyze the relationship between countries, their political regime types, and population sizes. By comparing data from 1950 and 2000, we will explore how countries' political systems and populations have changed over the 50-year period. Our goal is to identify patterns, trends, and potential relationships between population growth and changes in political regimes across different countries.

QUESTIONS

- How have political regime types across countries changed between1950 and 2000?
- What is the relationship between a country's population size and its political regime type?
- How have population sizes changed between countries with different political regime types from 1950 to 2000, and are there any noticeable patterns or trends?

INSPIRATION

Our team chose this topic because we have each experienced or grown up under different types of political regimes throughout our lifetimes. These personal experiences sparked our curiosity about how political systems differ across countries and how they evolve over time. We wanted to explore how government structures relate to population size and how these patterns have changed between 1950 and 2000. By combining our different perspectives with data visualization and analysis, we hope to better understand the relationship between population and political regimes around the world.

CONFLICTS RESOLUTION

If we have a conflict the team member can tell the team first. We’ll first adjust the workload or deadline if possible. If the member misses a deadline without communicating, the team will contact them and redistribute urgent tasks to other team members so the project can continue. Repeated problems will be documented and discussed with Amin if necessary. 

The team will try to make decisions through discussion. If the team is 50/50, each side will briefly explain its reasoning. If we still can’t agree, we’ll choose the option that best satisfies the assignment requirement. As a final solution, the team may use a majority vote, ask TA for feedback, or allow the person responsible for that part of the project to make the final decision.
